column7: note
/auth/mfa/verify shares the cluster-wide DB-backed login rate limiter (ADR-040), not unlimited
guardLastAdminDeactivation asks about the TARGET's admin status, not the acting caller's PAT restriction
SuspendInactiveUsers' admin-skip check is immune to the triggering caller's own PAT restriction

ADR-102's open system.write blast-radius decision is resolved by ADR-110 (deletion + reviewed per-route scope); every system.write gate site must appear in the reviewed allowlist, replacing ADR-102's age-based tripwire
login rate limiting blocks at LoginMaxAttempts within LoginWindow and expires correctly

SURFACE REMOVED (ADR-108 Phase 6 step 14b-2): proving test TestRateLimit_RemoteStorageGenuinelyThrottles deleted along with RemoteStorage itself; the property (a cluster-wide login rate limit genuinely throttling across a real RemoteStorage hop) is moot now that no RemoteStorage hop exists. ADR-040-RATELIMIT-BUDGET-WINDOW (same file) still covers the underlying rate-limit budget/window logic against the sole remaining backend.
an older binary refuses to start against a database migrated by a newer schema epoch
currentSchemaEpoch (3) and minCompatibleSchemaEpoch (2) have not changed without an explicit compatibility-floor decision
a machine identity can never be granted a role at global scope
no tracked source reintroduces the removed mlockall syscall from server startup

two OS processes migrating the same SQLite file (via a symlinked path, or with the sidecar lock deleted) are serialized by SQLite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, exactly one performs the fresh install, and the schema ends intact
a corrupt (non-integer) schema_epoch refuses boot via CreateStorage, across value shapes a lenient parser would accept, and leaves the database untouched

each soft-deleted user/project/environment/secret is purged on its own deleted_at against real storage: no cascade down to live/in-window children, no gating of expired children on their parent; TestPurgeExpiredSoftDeletes_EachEntityTypePurgedAlone covers per-type orchestration gating
repo-wide go/ast sweep: every raw/Table/Joins/subquery SQL reference to secret_nodes filters deleted_at or is allowlisted with a reason; flags all six ADR-033 historical sites on the pre-fix tree

expiry/suspension/restricted-MFA-step-up/access-schedule secret-read guards deny on every REST and gRPC value path for session and machine principals; automates ADR-105 "What is not wrong" manual trace (INV-GRPC-01)
a binary below the recorded minCompatibleEpoch floor (or facing a newer epoch with no floor recorded, or a corrupt floor) refuses to start before any migration step
an additive-safe migration does not raise the compatibility floor, and a breaking one does
recordSchemaEpoch never lowers a recorded schema epoch or compatibility floor

a machine identity bulk-approving an access request is subject to the escalation-by-proxy ceiling on its OWN machine-resolved permissions: the acting machine identity is derived from the real actor, not hardcoded to 0, so a machine caller is never reported to the ceiling as the trusted system pseudo-actor (ADR-030 gives a machine no UserID, making actorID==0 ambiguous)

every call site in internal/core and server/ that passes a literal false/0 for an actor-kind companion parameter carries a reviewed row explaining why no machine actor can reach it; a new unreviewed one fails the build, covering the class behind four separate findings (#1524 #1542 #1545 #2495)

the last-install-admin guards derive admin-ness from models.Role.BypassesPermissionChecks, not a name list: a flag-carrying role named outside the retired super_admin/admin/system_admin list is admin-conferring, so removing the installs last such global grant is refused (closes ADR-084s own "Not yet done" residual, INV-CORE-20)

every canonical admin-role-name string literal in internal/core non-test source carries a reviewed row saying it is not an admin-ness authority; a new unreviewed one fails the build, which is the mechanism that was missing when installAdminRoleIDSet survived ADR-084 for a month

a live SQLite connection reports PRAGMA synchronous = FULL (2), read back through a SECOND connection via OpenGormDB so it is a property of every connection this codebase opens -- the fast audit mode is PostgreSQL-only and has no SQLite branch at all

the SQLite DSN builder says _synchronous=FULL unconditionally and contains no NORMAL branch, and the setting may not change any other pragma either (#436 foreign keys, #465 busy timeout and WAL, #1996 BEGIN IMMEDIATE all still present)

no non-test Go file outside internal/config/config.go assigns storage.database.audit_durability or its deprecated alias insecure_audit_skip_durable_sync (ADR-112 Amendment 3); YAML unmarshal is the only write path, so no HTTP handler or gRPC RPC can change audit durability
no KEYORIX_* environment variable names audit durability anywhere in the main module, and a config naming neither key gets the backend default (strict on SQLite)

with the fast audit mode in effect on Postgres, an audit row that cannot be WRITTEN still fails the call; only the wait for the disk sync is skipped. pg-gated deliberately: on SQLite the flag is inert so the same test would pass with the mode off, which coordinator review of #2828 caught

AST-derived over every LocalStorage composite literal in the package, so a clone site added in future is covered the moment it is written: none except the root constructor may set auditSkipDurableSync, because a clone appends audit inside the CALLER transaction where SET LOCAL would relax the caller mutation. Positive controls assert exactly one constructor literal and at least two clone sites so the walk cannot pass vacuously

the behavioural half of the clone guard: exercises the real WithTransaction and reads the field off the clone it actually hands a caller, which is the shape the AST walk cannot see (a whole-struct copy would carry the field and is not a composite literal)

under Postgres async commit a committed audit row is immediately VISIBLE and only its durability lags, so consecutive appends still link and the chain still verifies. Asserts the SET LOCAL was actually issued first, so the linkage assertions cannot hold trivially on a durable commit

on Postgres the audit transaction issues no synchronous_commit statement at all when the mode is off (so the commit keeps the cluster's durable default) and exactly SET LOCAL synchronous_commit = off when it is on; the off case also asserts the test cluster's own synchronous_commit is on, so "we send nothing" genuinely means "the commit is durable"

synchronous_commit is back to on, on the same pooled connection, after the audit transaction commits -- SET LOCAL is transaction-scoped so the relaxation cannot follow the connection into the next transaction, which is where a secret WRITE would run

SIGKILLing the postmaster mid-write (the only event that can lose an async commit on Postgres) leaves a clean TAIL loss and a chain that still verifies. MANUAL by construction: it kills a database server, so it is gated on KX_FASTAUDIT_PG_CRASH_CONTAINER and skips in every automated run. Artefact: the run recorded in FASTAUDIT-1's PR body -- 70 acknowledged async commits, 3 lost as a clean tail starting at #67, VerifyAuditChain VALID over the 67 survivors

pins the reachability condition the remote not-in-effect branch rests on: storage.type remote is rejected unconditionally for a server config (ADR-083 validateRemoteStorageNotServer), so the posture report can never observe the configured-but-ignored state. If remote ever becomes server-reachable this goes red and the posture test gains its missing arm

a SQLite backend set to audit_durability: standard (by name or via the deprecated insecure_audit_skip_durable_sync: true) fails config validation with the exact named error (Amendment 1's SQLite rejection, kept by Amendment 3); strict, an explicit false alias and no setting still validate on SQLite
both audit_durability levels validate on postgres/postgresql, so a mutation that rejected standard unconditionally cannot hide behind the SQLite refusal test

GET /system/info's security.audit_durability carries the EFFECTIVE level: standard for a default PostgreSQL install, strict when set or on SQLite, the deprecated alias's mapping otherwise (ADR-112 Amendment 3)

the real built server binary, and admin validate/diagnose, exit non-zero with the named refusal on a SQLite config set to audit_durability: standard or insecure_audit_skip_durable_sync: true; the same config before the one-line edit works

real binary on real PostgreSQL: a default install logs the standard INFO line and admin validate reports standard; switching to strict between two starts logs the strict line and writes one security.posture_setting_changed event standard -> strict; no admin.audit_durable_sync_skipped_at_startup event; verify-audit VALID

a default SQLite install boots strict and logs one INFO line saying so, admin validate reports strict, the deprecated key is never mentioned, no per-start audit-durability event is written, and verify-audit is VALID
a break-glass activation can be reviewed exactly once; a second attempt is refused, not a silent overwrite
under real concurrent Postgres connections, exactly one of N racing review submissions for the same activation wins

the user who activated break-glass can never review their own activation, and an unattributable actor (actorID==0: a machine identity, or an unauthenticated local-CLI invocation) can never record a review at all. ADR-112 keeps activation single-person BECAUSE an independent post-activation review follows it, so a self-review collapses that two-person property into one person. There is no co-approver to also exclude (BreakGlassActivation carries no approver field and ADR-112 rejects two-person break-glass); TestBreakGlassActivation_HasNoApproverField guards that premise so adding co-approval later forces this exclusion to be revisited

a still-active activation cannot be reviewed; it must be revoked or expired first, so a reviewer is never asked to assess access that is still in use and a recorded review never reads as a closed item for an unfinished event. State is a read-time projection, so a TTL-lapsed activation already reads expired here and this refusal cannot strand a review behind a transition nobody performs

an activation with no recorded review, already older than break_glass.review_window, is counted as a deviation in the compliance posture report, together with the age of the worst outstanding one and the window it was measured against. This is exactly and only what ADR-112's every activation must be reviewed afterwards means (its own words: an open activation without a recorded review shows as a posture deviation) -- visibility, plus RunBreakGlassReviewReminder's recurring warning and audit event. A still-active unreviewed activation is counted too, since the ADR says an OPEN activation and ReviewBreakGlass refuses to review one that is still active. A pending review never blocks break-glass ACTIVATION itself (INV-CORE-break-glass-unreviewed-reported-never-blocks-activation, narrowed #2461 round 2) -- that scoping does not forbid a future, separately-decided, opt-in enforcement elsewhere

the "emergency-access" compliance control reports a real Gap when any activation is unreviewed past the window, not merely an informational count in Detail -- #2461 round 2, Andrei's decision item (b)
the periodic overdue-review reminder actively notifies each affected project's approver-role admins, not only a log line and an audit event -- #2461 round 2, Andrei's decision item (b)

a deployment with at most one active global admin-tier holder flags EmergencyAccess.IndependentReviewImpossible as its own distinct posture finding, rather than silently reading identical to "reviewed" or to an ordinary unreviewed backlog -- INV-CORE-break-glass-independent-review-impossible-is-visible, #2461 round 2, Andrei's decision item (c)

retention purge never hard-deletes a concluded, unreviewed activation no matter how old, so the posture deviation it represents cannot be silently erased by the passage of time before anyone reviews it
